meaning: The athletic stance a fielder is in as the pitch arrives: feet wider than the shoulders, knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet, hands out front.
example_en: Get in your ready position before the pitch.
example_es: Ponte en posición de listo antes del lanzamiento.
region_note: 'Posición de listo' itself not confirmed in a Spanish baseball source; EFDeportes (Cuba) uses 'listo para fildear'.

meaning: Keep the knees bent and the body and glove low to the ground while fielding.
example_en: Stay low and let the ball come to you.
example_es: Quédate abajo y deja que la bola llegue.

meaning: Keep the head and glove down through the catch; do not pop up before the ball is in the glove.
example_en: Stay down on that ball, you came up early.
example_es: No te levantes con esa bola, te paraste temprano.
region_note: Phrasal verb: Spanish speakers may say 'stay below' or 'stay in the low'.

es_alt: peso en la punta de los pies
meaning: Body weight on the front of the feet, not the heels, so the fielder can move quickly.
example_en: Weight forward, you're on your heels.
example_es: El peso hacia adelante, estás en los talones.

meaning: Small walking steps toward the plate as the pitcher delivers, so the fielder is moving when the ball is hit.
example_en: Creep in, then land as the ball gets to the zone.
example_es: Da tus pasitos y cae cuando la bola llegue a la zona.
region_note: No confirmed Spanish term; gloss descriptively.

meaning: The timed hop or step at the end of the creep that lands as the ball reaches the hitting zone. Also called a ready step.
example_en: Time your prep step with the swing.
example_es: Coordina tu paso de preparación con el swing.
region_note: Spanish term unverified.

meaning: Hands and glove held in front of the body, where the fielder can see the ball into the glove.
example_en: Hands out front, see it into the glove.
example_es: Las manos al frente, mira la bola hasta el guante.

meaning: How a player moves and places the feet to field and throw.
example_en: Your footwork was much better today.
example_es: Tu juego de pies estuvo mucho mejor hoy.

meaning: Cue to get the feet moving to the ball instead of reaching with the glove.
example_en: Move your feet, don't reach for it.
example_es: Mueve los pies, no te estires por ella.
region_note: English uses 'your feet', not 'the feet'.

meaning: Start moving the feet early and keep them active.
example_en: Get your feet moving before the ball gets to you.
example_es: Mueve los pies antes de que la bola te llegue.

meaning: The first move after the ball is hit; it should be quick and in the right direction.
example_en: Good first step on that one.
example_es: Buen primer paso en esa.

meaning: The way a player or throw is moving; also the target the body should line up toward.
example_en: Your first step went the wrong direction.
example_es: Tu primer paso fue en la dirección equivocada.

meaning: The path a fielder takes to the ball relative to its line; a good angle cuts the ball off.
example_en: Take an angle so you cut the ball off.
example_es: Toma un ángulo para cortarle el paso a la bola.

meaning: Correction: approach the ball on a more efficient path, usually cutting in front of it rather than going straight sideways.
example_en: Take a better angle, you let it play you.
example_es: Toma un mejor ángulo, dejaste que la bola te jugara.
region_note: 'Coger' is vulgar in Mexico and Argentina; fine in the Caribbean.

meaning: Get the feet in a balanced, lined-up position before throwing.
example_en: Set your feet and make a good throw.
example_es: Planta los pies y haz un buen tiro.
region_note: Spanish equivalents unverified.

meaning: Cue to move the feet into a throwing position after the catch instead of throwing flat-footed.
example_en: Feet to throw, don't just flip it.
example_es: Los pies para tirar, no la tires de cualquier forma.
region_note: Coaching shorthand; not a full sentence.

meaning: Short side steps, feet not crossing, used to move into a throwing position or to cover a few feet.
example_en: Shuffle your feet and throw.
example_es: Desplázate de lado y tira.
region_note: Spanish term unverified.

meaning: Turning and crossing one leg over the other to run sideways quickly.
example_en: Crossover and go, don't shuffle on a ball that far.
example_es: Cruza y arranca, no te desplaces de lado con una bola tan lejos.

meaning: An outfielder's first step back with the foot on the ball's side, opening the hips to run back on a ball hit over his head.
example_en: Drop step and go, don't backpedal.
example_es: Paso atrás y arranca, no corras de espaldas.
region_note: Spanish term unverified.

meaning: Do not run backward facing the infield; turn and run instead.
example_en: Don't backpedal, turn and run.
example_es: No corras de espaldas, voltéate y corre.

meaning: Turn the hips toward where you are going so you can run.
example_en: Open your hips and go get it.
example_es: Abre la cadera y ve a buscarla.

meaning: Catch or stop a batted ball, especially a ground ball, and get control of it.
example_en: Field the ball first, then worry about the throw.
example_es: Fildea la bola primero, después piensa en el tiro.
region_note: 'Fildear' is a common loanword (field). Formal Spanish prefers 'atrapar'.

meaning: Take a thrown or batted ball in the air with the glove. For a ground ball, coaches usually say 'field' instead of 'catch'.
example_en: Catch it with two hands, then throw.
example_es: Atrápala con las dos manos, después tira.
region_note: 'Coger' is vulgar in Mexico and Argentina. 'Cachar' is recorded in the Diccionario del español dominicano for the catcher's catch (via a secondary source).

meaning: A batted ball that rolls or bounces along the ground. Also called a grounder.
example_en: We'll take fifty ground balls today.
example_es: Hoy vamos a coger cincuenta roletazos.
region_note: 'Rolin' is recorded in the Diccionario del español dominicano; 'rolling' is used in Cuba.

meaning: A batted ball hit high in the air.
example_en: Call every fly ball loud.
example_es: Pide en voz alta cada elevado.
region_note: 'Flai' is the Caribbean adaptation of 'fly'.

meaning: A short, high fly ball, usually in or near the infield.
example_en: That pop-up is yours, call it.
example_es: Ese elevado es tuyo, pídelo.
region_note: 'Palomita' is regional; unverified for DR.

meaning: A ball hit hard and low on a flat path.
example_en: React to the line drive, don't guess.
example_es: Reacciona a la línea, no adivines.
region_note: Spanish terms from compiler knowledge, unverified here.

meaning: Run in aggressively toward a slow or routine ground ball instead of waiting for it.
example_en: Charge the ball, don't let it play you.
example_es: Ataca la bola, no dejes que ella te juegue a ti.
region_note: 'Charge' here is not 'cobrar' (a false friend).

meaning: Cue to move forward and take the ball rather than wait on it.
example_en: Come get it! Be aggressive.
example_es: ¡Ven a buscarla! Sé agresivo.

es: trabaja a través de la bola
es_alt: sigue moviéndote a través de la bola
meaning: Keep moving through the catch toward the target so fielding and throwing are one motion; don't stop on the ball.
example_en: Work through the ball and toward first.
example_es: Sigue moviéndote a través de la bola hacia primera.
region_note: No standard Spanish equivalent found; gloss by demonstration.

meaning: Field the ball in front of the body where you can see it, not under or beside you.
example_en: Glove out front, you're catching it under your body.
example_es: El guante al frente, la estás cogiendo debajo del cuerpo.

meaning: Put the glove on or near the ground early, so you come up with the ball rather than going down after it.
example_en: Get your glove down early.
example_es: Baja el guante temprano.
region_note: English uses 'your glove', not 'the glove', in direct cues.

meaning: After the catch, bring the glove and ball up into the belly area to start the transfer.
example_en: Catch it and funnel it to your belly.
example_es: Atrápala y llévala al estómago.
region_note: Spanish equivalent unverified.

meaning: Relaxed hands that give with the ball so it stays in the glove.
example_en: Soft hands, let the ball in.
example_es: Manos suaves, deja que la bola entre.

meaning: Fielding a ball on the throwing-hand side by reaching across the body with the glove turned over.
example_en: Take that one on the backhand.
example_es: Coge esa de revés.

meaning: Fielding a ball on the glove side with the glove open, palm toward the ball.
example_en: Forehand, open glove, use your feet.
example_es: Por el lado del guante, guante abierto, usa los pies.
region_note: Spanish equivalent unverified.

meaning: Catching a ground ball right after it bounces, close to the ground; also the bounce itself.
example_en: Pick the short hop, don't let it eat you up.
example_es: Coge el bote corto, no dejes que te coma.
region_note: No Spanish term confirmed; 'bote corto' and 'medio bote' are unverified.

meaning: An unexpected bounce of a ground ball.
example_en: Bad hop, nothing you could do.
example_es: Mal bote, no podías hacer nada.

meaning: Judge how the ground ball will bounce and adjust your feet to get a good hop.
example_en: Read the hop and pick a good one.
example_es: Lee el bote y escoge uno bueno.

es: mira la bola hasta el guante
es_alt: sigue la bola hasta el guante
meaning: Watch the ball all the way into the glove.
example_en: See it into the glove, then throw.
example_es: Mira la bola hasta el guante, después tira.

en: keep your eyes on the ball
es: no le quites la vista a la bola
meaning: Keep watching the ball.
example_en: Keep your eyes on the ball the whole way.
example_es: No le quites la vista a la bola en todo el recorrido.
region_note: English uses 'your eyes', not 'the eyes'.

meaning: Move so the body is behind the ball, blocking it and lined up to throw.
example_en: Get your body behind it, don't stab at it.
example_es: Ponte detrás de la bola, no le tires el guante.
region_note: Phrasal verb 'get behind'; Spanish speakers may say 'put behind'.

meaning: Field the ball with the throwing hand, without the glove, usually on a slow roller.
example_en: Only bare-hand it if it's stopped or slow.
example_es: Cógela a mano pelada solo si está parada o va lenta.

meaning: Stop the ball even if you can't field it cleanly, so it does not get past you.
example_en: If you can't catch it, keep it in front.
example_es: Si no la puedes coger, que no se te pase.

meaning: A misplay that the official scorer judges an average fielder should have made into an out. In baseball English you 'make' or 'commit' an error.
example_en: Forget the error, next ball.
example_es: Olvida el error, a la próxima.
region_note: 'Commit an error' is correct in baseball English, but 'commit a mistake' is not. 'Pifia' is colloquial in some countries; unverified for DR.

meaning: Send the ball to a teammate with the arm. Use 'pitch' only for the pitcher.
example_en: Make a good, strong throw to first.
example_es: Haz un tiro bueno y fuerte a primera.
region_note: 'Lanzar' also means 'pitch'; in English 'throw' covers fielders.

meaning: Throw the ball to first base. No article and normally no 'base': 'to first', 'to second', 'to third'.
example_en: Field it and throw to first.
example_es: Fildéala y tira a primera.
region_note: Spanish speakers may say 'to the first base'.

meaning: Moving the ball quickly from the glove to the throwing hand.
example_en: Quick transfer, get it out of the glove.
example_es: Cambio rápido, saca la bola del guante.
region_note: Spanish term unverified.

meaning: A clear line from thrower to receiver, with no runner or fielder in the way.
example_en: Step off the line and clear your throwing lane.
example_es: Sal de la línea y limpia tu línea de tiro.
region_note: Spanish term unverified.

meaning: An outfielder's hop and step after the catch that turns momentum into a strong throw.
example_en: Catch it coming in, crow hop and throw.
example_es: Atrápala viniendo hacia adelante, haz el crow hop y tira.
region_note: Spanish calque 'salto de cuervo' unverified; the English term may be used as-is.

meaning: Throw on a line through the cutoff man so he can catch it or let it go.
example_en: Hit the cutoff, keep it low.
example_es: Dale al cortador, mantenla baja.
region_note: Spanish terms unverified.

meaning: Throw on a low line so the cutoff can handle it and the ball gets there fast.
example_en: Keep it low through the cutoff.
example_es: Mantenla baja a través del cortador.

meaning: A throw meant to bounce once before reaching the base, usually from the outfield.
example_en: One hop to the bag is fine.
example_es: De un bote a la base está bien.

meaning: The fielder, or the play, that takes an outfielder's throw and can redirect or stop it.
example_en: Who's the cutoff on a single to right?
example_es: ¿Quién es el cortador en un sencillo al right?
region_note: Spanish terms unverified; the English term may be used as-is.

meaning: A two-throw play: an infielder goes out to take a long outfield throw and relays it to a base.
example_en: Line up the relay, he's going for three.
example_es: Alinea el relevo, va para tercera.
region_note: Caution: Insinga gives 'relevo' = bullpen, so the Spanish gloss is ambiguous.

meaning: A call telling the cutoff man to catch the throw (often followed by the base: 'Cut two!').
example_en: Cut! Cut two!
example_es: ¡Corta! ¡Corta y a segunda!
region_note: Call wording varies by team.

meaning: A call telling the cutoff man not to touch the throw.
example_en: Let it go! Let it go!
example_es: ¡Déjala pasar! ¡Déjala!
region_note: Call wording varies by team.

meaning: A play that records two outs.
example_en: Two outs on one play, that's a double play.
example_es: Dos outs en una jugada, eso es un doble play.

meaning: Complete a double play.
example_en: Get two, turn two!
example_es: ¡Saca dos, haz el doble!
region_note: 'Virar' unverified.

meaning: Call meaning a double play is on, or 'throw to second'.
example_en: Runner on first, nobody out, think two!
example_es: Corredor en primera, sin outs, ¡piensa en dos!

meaning: The toss or throw a middle infielder gives to the man covering second on a double play.
example_en: Give him a good feed, chest high.
example_es: Dale una buena bola, a la altura del pecho.
region_note: Spanish equivalent unverified.

meaning: The footwork at second base to receive the feed, touch the bag and throw to first.
example_en: Work on your pivot at second.
example_es: Trabaja tu pivote en segunda.
region_note: Spanish term unverified.

meaning: Go to a base to take a throw.
example_en: Shortstop, cover the bag on the steal.
example_es: Short, cubre la base en el robo.

meaning: Stand behind the base or fielder in line with the throw, in case the ball gets past. Also means 'move backward' as a plain instruction.
example_en: Right fielder, back up first on every ground ball.
example_es: Right, respalda primera en cada roletazo.
region_note: Two meanings: 'back up first' (support) vs 'back up!' (move back). Spanish 'respaldar' unverified for field use.

meaning: Judging where a batted ball is going (height, speed, direction) from the moment it is hit.
example_en: Good read off the bat.
example_es: Buena lectura del batazo.

meaning: The path an outfielder runs to the ball.
example_en: Take a straight route, you drifted.
example_es: Toma una ruta directa, te fuiste de lado.

meaning: Outfield: get a step behind where the ball will land so you catch it moving toward your throw.
example_en: Get behind the ball so you can come through it.
example_es: Ponte detrás de la bola para venir hacia adelante.
region_note: Phrasal-verb chunk; teach with demonstration.

meaning: Run forward toward the infield (for a short fly ball, or to play shallower).
example_en: Come in! It's falling short.
example_es: ¡Ven! Se está quedando corta.
region_note: Spanish uses one verb (entrar/venir); English uses verb + particle.

meaning: Run back toward the fence.
example_en: Go back, go back, it's over your head!
example_es: ¡Atrás, atrás, va por encima!

meaning: The space between two outfielders (left-center or right-center).
example_en: Cut that ball off in the gap.
example_es: Córtale esa bola en la brecha.
region_note: Spanish terms unverified; 'hueco' is attested for the infield 'hole' [29].

meaning: The space between the shortstop and third baseman (or between first and second).
example_en: Backhand in the hole, plant and throw.
example_es: De revés en el hueco, planta y tira.

meaning: Call meaning 'I am catching this ball; everyone else clear out'. Call it loud and more than once.
example_en: I got it! I got it!
example_es: ¡La tengo! ¡La tengo!
region_note: Fixed form: 'I got it', not 'I have it' or 'I take it'.

meaning: Call some teams use for 'I'm catching it'.
example_en: Ball, ball, ball!
example_es: ¡Bola, bola, bola!
region_note: Varies by team.

meaning: Call meaning 'I am catching this'.
example_en: Mine! Mine!
example_es: ¡Mía! ¡Mía!

meaning: Call telling a teammate to make the play.
example_en: You, you! Take it!
example_es: ¡Tuya, tuya! ¡Cógela!
region_note: Common but not confirmed as standard in this review; treat as a team convention.

meaning: Fielders calling for balls and telling each other where to throw.
example_en: Communication wins those plays. Talk to each other.
example_es: La comunicación gana esas jugadas. Háblense.

meaning: Which fielder has the right to a ball both can reach (e.g. the center fielder over the corners, outfielders over infielders).
example_en: Center fielder has priority, so get out of his way.
example_es: El center tiene prioridad, apártate.

meaning: Say the call loudly to claim a ball.
example_en: If you can get there, call it.
example_es: Si llegas, pídela.

meaning: Where a fielder stands before the pitch, based on the hitter, count and situation.
example_en: Check your positioning before every pitch.
example_es: Revisa tu posicionamiento antes de cada lanzamiento.

meaning: Move a few steps toward one side from normal position.
example_en: Shade him to pull a couple of steps.
example_es: Córrete un par de pasos hacia su lado de halar.
region_note: Spanish terms unverified.

meaning: How deep or shallow a fielder plays ('double-play depth', 'in', 'back').
example_en: Double-play depth, two steps in.
example_es: Profundidad de doble play, dos pasos adentro.

meaning: A hitter who usually hits to his own side of the field (left side for a right-handed hitter).
example_en: He's a pull hitter, cheat over a step.
example_es: Es bateador de halar, córrete un paso.
region_note: 'Halar' (Caribbean) unverified in a cited source.

meaning: Moving fielders away from standard spots for a hitter. Since 2023 MLB requires four players on the infield dirt and two infielders on each side of second at the pitch.
example_en: No full shift anymore. Two on each side of the bag.
example_es: Ya no hay shift completo. Dos a cada lado de la base.
region_note: Gender of the loanword varies; unverified.

meaning: The leather glove a fielder wears. Use 'mitt' for the catcher's or first baseman's.
example_en: Glove up, let's go.
example_es: Guante puesto, vamos.

meaning: The side of the body where the glove is (left side for a right-handed thrower).
example_en: That ball's to your glove side, forehand it.
example_es: Esa bola va por el lado del guante, cógela de frente.

es_alt: el lado de la mano de tirar
meaning: The side of the body of the throwing arm.
example_en: Ball to your throwing side, backhand it.
example_es: Bola por tu lado de tirar, cógela de revés.

meaning: Lower the body by bending the knees, not the back.
example_en: Bend your knees, not your back.
example_es: Dobla las rodillas, no la espalda.
region_note: English uses 'your knees'; 'the knees' sounds like a manual.

meaning: Start the drill; also general encouragement.
example_en: Okay, let's go, first group.
example_es: Bueno, vamos, primer grupo.

meaning: Go back to the starting position for the next rep.
example_en: Good. Reset.
example_es: Bien. A tu posición.

meaning: Do the rep again.
example_en: Good, again.
example_es: Bien, otra vez.

meaning: Do it again after a mistake.
example_en: No problem, try again.
example_es: No hay problema, inténtalo otra vez.

meaning: Repeat once more.
example_en: One more time, stay down.
example_es: Una vez más, quédate abajo.

meaning: Announce the number of reps left.
example_en: Let's do three more and get water.
example_es: Vamos a hacer tres más y a tomar agua.

meaning: Final rep of the drill.
example_en: Last one, make it a good one.
example_es: La última, que sea buena.

meaning: There is no hurry; do it under control.
example_en: You've got time, take your time and make a good throw.
example_es: Tienes tiempo, tómatelo y haz un buen tiro.

meaning: One repetition of a drill.
example_en: Every rep counts.
example_es: Cada repetición cuenta.

meaning: Get into a line for a drill.
example_en: Line up behind the bag.
example_es: Hagan fila detrás de la base.

meaning: Gather the players around the coach.
example_en: Bring it in, everybody.
example_es: Vengan todos, júntense.
region_note: Not about the ball: it means 'come here as a group'.

meaning: Introduce a demonstration.
example_en: Watch me first, then you try.
example_es: Mírame primero, después lo intentas tú.

meaning: Tell a player it's his turn in the drill.
example_en: Okay, your turn.
example_es: Bueno, te toca.

meaning: General praise; best followed by what was good.
example_en: Nice job, you stayed down.
example_es: Buen trabajo, te quedaste abajo.

meaning: Confirms the player did exactly what was asked.
example_en: That's it! That's the footwork.
example_es: ¡Eso es! Ese es el juego de pies.

meaning: The rep improved; usually followed by the next cue.
example_en: Better. Now get your feet set.
example_es: Mejor. Ahora planta los pies.

meaning: Checks understanding of an explanation. A demonstration ('Show me') is a better check.
example_en: Catch it out front so you can see it. Does that make sense?
example_es: Atrápala al frente para verla. ¿Me entiendes?
region_note: Literal 'tiene sentido' is acceptable, but '¿me entiendes?' is closer in feel.

meaning: Ask the player to demonstrate, to check understanding.
example_en: Show me your ready position.
example_es: Enséñame tu posición de listo.

meaning: Asks the player to describe the rep, building self-assessment.
example_en: What did you feel there? Were you on your heels?
example_es: ¿Qué sentiste ahí? ¿Estabas en los talones?

meaning: Successfully field and throw for the out. English uses 'make', not 'do'.
example_en: Make the routine play every time.
example_es: Haz la jugada de rutina cada vez.
region_note: Make vs do: Spanish 'hacer' covers both.

meaning: An ordinary play an average fielder is expected to make.
example_en: Make the routine play first.
example_es: Primero haz la jugada de rutina.

meaning: Forget the last play and focus on the next one.
example_en: Shake it off, next ball.
example_es: Olvídalo, a la próxima.
